newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo aluminium futures end lower with LME, dollar.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo aluminium futures end lower with LME, dollar.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based aluminium futures closed lower across the board on Wednesday as the metal's decline on the London Metal Exchange (LME) and the dollar's retreat triggered selling, traders said.
"Sentiment is not bad, but people are squaring positions to cover losses made in the precious metals market." added a trader at one of Japan's major trading houses.

Many individual investors, who account for most of the trade on the Tokyo Commodity Exchange (TOCOM), have suffered serious losses on short positions in the precious metals market, where prices for the platinum group metals have remained high despite the resumption of Russian exports.
The June aluminium contract shed 4.2 yen to close at 201.8 yen per kg, while April lost 4.0 yen to end at 204.0 yen. Other contracts were down from 1.5 to 3.7 yen. Estimated volume was 2,320 lots.
The dollar was quoted around 119 yen in late Asia trade, after trading well below the 119 yen level the previous day.

On the Tokyo precious metals market, which continued to be the focus of individual investors, most palladium contracts ended down their daily limits after opening at their limit highs. Platinum also finished at its limit lows.
In London overnight, LME benchmark three-month aluminium shed $23 to $1,721 a tonne, in what traders regarded as a needed correction after a strong rally since last week.
